[2026-05-19 20:30] All 5 probes complete. Handbook updated at `docs/migration/entu-schema-mutation-handbook.md`. All probe entities cleaned up (all returned `{"deleted":true}`).

---

## P1 — Formula re-aggregation (§5.1)

| Observation | Result |
|---|---|
| GET instances immediately after formula definition change | Stale — computed shows old value, no automatic recompute |
| Re-save one instance (touch any field) | Computed updates immediately on that instance only. Other instances remain stale. |
| Probe `/recalculate`, `/reindex`, `/aggregate`, `/recalc`, `/recompute`, `/formula/recalculate` | All 404 — no bulk re-aggregation API endpoint exists |

**Verdict:** Formula changes require a full per-instance backfill-touch pass. No shortcut. Ask Argo whether an internal (non-API-public) endpoint exists — this affects Phase A/B timeline. §5.1 and §3 updated with this.

---

## P3 — Entity type rename impact (§5.3)

| Observation | Result |
|---|---|
| `_type[0].reference` after rename | Unchanged — always points to same type entity ID |
| `_type[0].string` immediately after rename | Shows OLD name (race window) |
| `_type[0].string` after ~1 second | Updated to new name |
| `?_type.string=<new-name>` query | Finds instances after ~1s propagation |
| `?_type.string=<old-name>` query | Finds instances immediately, returns 0 after propagation |
| `?_type.reference=<id>` query | Always finds instances — unaffected by rename |

**Verdict:** Entity type rename is **FREE** — no data migration required on instances. The string denormalization is an auto-maintained Entu cache. Migration scripts should use `?_type.reference=<id>` to avoid the ~1s window. §5.3 updated.

---

## P4 — Cascade on entity type delete (§5.4)

| Observation | Result |
|---|---|
| DELETE entity type | `{"deleted":true}` — succeeds immediately |
| GET instance after type deleted | 200 — full entity body returned. `_type[0]` preserved (ref + stale string). |
| `?_type.reference=<deleted-id>` query | 0 results — orphans invisible to type queries |
| `?_type.string=_probe_canary` query | 0 results — invisible |
| POST to orphaned instance | Succeeds — instance is editable |
| DELETE orphaned instance | `{"deleted":true}` — deletable |

**Verdict:** Confirmed — deleting a type entity creates silent orphans. They persist forever, readable/editable/deletable only by known `_id`. Invisible to all type queries. The §2.7 "rename to `_DEPRECATED_*`" recommendation is correct and now evidence-backed. §5.4 updated.

---

## P5 — Bulk property-value delete API (§5.5)

| Form | Status |
|---|---|
| `DELETE /property?ids=<id1>,<id2>` | 404 — route not found |
| `DELETE /property` with JSON body `{"ids":[...]}` | 404 — route not found |
| `DELETE /property/<id1>,<id2>` (path comma) | **500 Server Error** — route exists but fails; properties NOT deleted |
| `DELETE /properties` (plural) | 404 — route not found |
| `POST /entity/{id}` with `[{"_id": "<prop-id>", "deleted": true}]` | 400 "Property type not set" — rejected |

**Verdict:** No working bulk delete. Strictly serial: `DELETE /property/{single-id}` only. At 50ms/call, 104k properties ≈ **87 minutes** for a full backfill pass. Strong argument for asking Argo if there's an internal bulk endpoint. §5.5 updated.

---

## P6 — `_sharing` semantics (§5.6)

Tested on instances with explicit `_sharing` property set at creation:

| `_sharing` value | GET with JWT | GET with no auth header |
|---|---|---|
| `public` | 200 ✓ | 200 ✓ — full entity data visible |
| `private` | 200 ✓ | 403 "No accessible properties" |
| `domain` | 200 ✓ | 403 "No accessible properties" |

Additional findings:
- `/polyphony/public/entity/{id}` → 404 (no such route). Public entities are served at the standard `/entity/{id}` endpoint, just without auth requirement.
- `_sharing` set on an entity TYPE entity sets that type entity's own visibility — **not** a default for data instances. Data instances have no `_sharing` unless set explicitly at creation (default = effectively private).

**Verdict:** `public` = true unauthenticated internet access. `domain` and `private` = identical via API (both block unauthenticated requests). For Phase D: setting `organization._sharing=public` makes orgs readable to unauthenticated clients (federation). v4E mapping confirmed. §5.6 updated.

---

## 2 New Gaps Found (§6 rows 9–10)

**Gap 9:** `_sharing` not inherited by data instances from entity type entity. This is a major operational surprise — setting `_sharing` on a type entity does not propagate to instances. Each instance needing non-default visibility must have `_sharing` set explicitly at creation.

**Gap 10:** No `/public/entity/` API path exists. Public access works on the same `/entity/{id}` endpoint with no auth header.

---

## Time Estimate

Probes took approximately 15 minutes wall-clock (I ran P1 setup serially due to needing formula syntax, then P3+P4+P5+P6 in parallel). The actual probe calls were fast — the latency was figuring out formula syntax and verifying "true" responses in P5 (they were routing to already-used IDs initially).

**For the Argo call decision:** Worth calling primarily on P5 (bulk delete) — that 87-minute serial estimate is the single biggest migration timeline risk. Secondarily P1 (bulk re-aggregation). P3/P4/P6 are fully resolved; no Argo needed for those.

JSON.stringify drops it, but the executor would POST `{type: 'label', string: undefined}` to Entu — likely fails the create.
- v4E property defs use `required: true`, NOT `mandatory: true`. The executor's `propertyToPayload` only checks `def.mandatory`, so every "required" property would silently lose its required-ness.
- v4E property defs also have `note`, `blurb`, `sharing`, `parents`, `reference_query` (Entu's `reference_query` shape is much richer too) — we'd need to decide which to forward.
